$comment: The browser suites. A third project rather than a widening of tsconfig.app.json / tsconfig.test.json, because browser-test code is the one place in this tree where DOM globals and node globals are both in scope but belong to DIFFERENT processes: `process` is the runner's, `document` is the browser's, and the two only meet inside a page.evaluate callback. Folding these files into the app project would put `process` in scope for application code that must never read it; folding them into the test project would hand vitest specs the Playwright globals and let a spec be written against the wrong runner. The build reference in tsconfig.json is what makes `npm run typecheck` cover both configs and both spec trees -- without it a config option can silently stop being passed.
